items.title: Google rolls back the needless AI generation tools it added to Google Earth
items.excerpt: Days after adding its Nano Banana generative-image tools to Google Earth, Google is pulling them back following user backlash that AI-invented renderings degraded a trusted mapping/visualization product. A concrete signal on the limits of dropping generative image AI into spatial-design and place-based visualization workflows.

items.title: Rebelle 8.3 proves the future of digital painting isn't AI, it's making brushes feel real
items.excerpt: Escape Motions' Rebelle 8.3 doubles down on physically realistic brush and watercolor simulation rather than generative AI, framing a deliberate craft-first counter-position in a design-tool market racing to bolt on AI. A useful read on where creative software is choosing simulation over generation.

items.title: Jakob's Law: how to apply it as AI collapses surfaces into one chat box
items.excerpt: As AI collapses distinct app surfaces and screens into a single conversational chat box, this piece reworks Jakob's Law of familiarity for generative UI - what patterns designers must preserve so users still feel oriented when the interface itself is generated on the fly.

items.title: Rethinking friction in an AI world
items.excerpt: A designer's argument that 'frictionless' is the wrong default once AI can do almost anything instantly - reframing where intentional friction should be added back into AI-driven products to keep users in control, and how that reshapes the design process.

items.title: Battling AI fatigue as a designer and developer: a practical guide
items.excerpt: A practical field guide to 'AI fatigue' in design and dev teams - concrete tactics for deciding when to reach for AI tooling versus when it adds noise, aimed at keeping an AI-saturated creative workflow sustainable rather than exhausting.
